findings.failureScenario: The spec for photo.copyMetadata lists only title, caption, copyright, creator, location and keywords. The code also copies altText, extendedDescription, city, state and country (library.rs:628-630). The `fields` enum for photo.pasteMetadata leaves those five keys out, yet the filter matches raw clipboard keys (library.rs:649). An agent that follows the spec and passes fields:["location"] to paste a place gets only the sublocation string; City, State and Country are silently left alone. Alt text and city/state/country can be pasted selectively only by guessing undocumented key names.
findings.action: List every copied key (altText, extendedDescription, city, state, country) in both spec strings, or have `location` expand to location, city, state and country in the paste filter.

findings.failureScenario: The photo.label spec marks `label` as required (`{label: red|...|none, ids?}`). The code treats a missing `label` the same as "none" (library.rs:733), so a control or agent call that misspells or omits the key (for example {"color":"red"}) succeeds and removes the colour label from every selected photo, with no error. The sibling folder.label command returns "missing `label`" for the same mistake (library.rs:491).
findings.action: Return an error when `label` is absent, as folder.label does, or document `label?` with absent meaning none.

findings.failureScenario: The module docs of the desktop app say the library comes from `--library`, else `$LIGHTCRAFT_LIBRARY`, else the last opened library. The resolver checks `EMBER_LIBRARY` first and falls back to `LIGHTCRAFT_LIBRARY` (library.rs:74-76). The inline comment at main.rs:824 leaves out the environment step entirely. A user who has both variables set (or only EMBER_LIBRARY) and reads the module docs or the comment will mispredict which library opens. The `--help` text in the same file does list both.
findings.action: Update the module docs and the comment at main.rs:824 to give the actual order: --library, EMBER_LIBRARY, LIGHTCRAFT_LIBRARY, saved library, then the default.
